scopeReview: IMP-6.C.1 and D.1: mixed uses, walkability, transit-oriented development, smart growth, New Urbanism, greenbelts and slow growth; intended access/livability benefits and possible housing, segregation or place-character concerns.
varietyReview: Four assessed stimuli compare straight-line/network distances, an original station-area plan, per-person versus aggregate travel and joint walking/rent indicators. Remaining cases evaluate specific initiatives, implementation and regional tradeoffs.
repetitionReview: Quantitative tasks use different denominators and causal limits; map requires interpreting access plus an evaluation. New applications avoid claiming a design label guarantees equity. Answer positions vary and explanations address each option; difficulty not empirically calibrated.
referenceNote: Official scope and primary EPA design/access descriptions checked. Scenarios, counts and diagram are original and hypothetical; no copied figures, new student resources or independent human-review claim.

questions.correctOption: Plan B has a walking route one-third as long, illustrating the importance of network connections.
questions.independentReview: Independently checked 300/900=1/3 and route/direct ratios 4.5 versus1.5. Route distance only, no assumption about walking speed, safety or causal health effects.

questions.correctOption: Measure transit and walking access alongside housing costs and who can remain or move into the area.
questions.independentReview: Map confirms homes/shops/station proximity only; question asks an evaluation, not proof of realized affordability or reduced driving. Plan is a hypothetical teaching abstraction without a claimed walk-distance scale. Browser geometry corrected before checkpoint: continuous route now passes exactly through station [50,30], with the Walk label anchored away from the Station label.

questions.correctOption: It rises from 1.2 million to 1.6 million vehicle-km/day.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed totals1.2m and1.6m; later/initial4/3. No emissions inferred because vehicle types/energy factors absent. Before/after association does not prove the plan caused the change.

questions.correctOption: Walking increased by 15 percentage points while median monthly rent increased by 200 currency units.
questions.independentReview: Independently checked35−20=15 percentage points,1000−800=200,relative ratios.75 and.25. No inference that the same residents were surveyed or all households face identical costs.

questions.correctOption: Mixed land use intended to bring different daily activities closer together.
questions.independentReview: Official C.1 mixed-use scope; no claim that every combination of industrial and residential activity is compatible or that proximity guarantees accessibility.

questions.correctOption: A walkable, connected neighborhood with a mix of uses and housing forms.
questions.independentReview: Verified broad New Urbanist features against CED/EPA. Distinguishes design principles from guaranteed social outcomes or a universal architectural style.

questions.correctOption: Development pressure may shift beyond the belt or affect housing costs if other conditions constrain supply.
questions.independentReview: No categorical claim that greenbelts always raise prices or cause leapfrog development. Retains both the intended open-space function and conditional spillover assessment.

questions.correctOption: Development is organized to support usable access to transit and nearby activities, including pedestrian connections.
questions.independentReview: Distinguishes actual access from nominal proximity; transportation-oriented term in framework is rendered with common transit-oriented usage, no fixed universal station radius.

questions.correctOption: Changes in development location, open space, housing availability and costs across the affected region.
questions.independentReview: No assumption that lower approvals necessarily protect every habitat or cause any fixed price change. Checks implementation-versus-outcome and municipal-versus-regional scale.

questions.correctOption: Rising costs or loss of valued local features may accompany the access improvements.
questions.independentReview: Matches D.1 benefits/criticisms without treating any criticism as an established outcome in a real place. Original application, no actual resident attribution.

questions.correctOption: Design rules interact with investment, housing policy, markets and transport service.
questions.independentReview: Separates zoning permission, realized construction and social outcomes. No real policy prescription, price guarantee or unverified causal statistic.
